native_result.query: How does the median wealth of white individuals compare to that of black and Hispanic individuals from 1985 onwards?
native_result.HypoA: 1985 onwards, white individuals have a significantly higher median wealth compared to black and Hispanic individuals.
native_result.HypoB: Since the earliest available snapshot (1985), the median family net wealth of white (Non-Black Non-Hispanic) individuals exceeds that of Black and Hispanic individuals in every wealth year observed (1985, 1990, 1996), by a factor that WIDENS from 2.2x to 4.3x vs Black and from 7.0x to 16.6x vs Hispanic; every year the ordering is White > Black > Hispanic, with Hispanic medians lagging due to a large zero/near-zero wealth share.

Metric = median family net wealth for the three wealth snapshots (1985, 1990, 1996 — the only wealth years present). Missingness = complete-case per year (n reported for every median) with a balanced-panel (all 3 years, n=5,739) robustness run because attrition is differential (White-proxy 52.6% missing in 1996). Negative/debt and zero wealth retained as valid observations (no trimming/floored). Bootstrap 95% CIs for medians. CPI-U sensitivity (1985/1990→1996 dollars) used only for growth-over-time statements; within-year group ratios are inflation-invariant. Unweighted: no weight column exists in the data, so results describe this NLSY79 sample.
